text:
Margo: noticed a weird tail latency spike on prometheus scrapers for the eu-west GPU fleet starting ~2017-03-01 09:12 UTC. remotes show lots of 504s from rw-proxy and remotes are backing up :grimacing:
Ashish: can you paste the prometheus logs / remote_write errors?
Margo: yep -- here's a representative snippet from one sidecar:
```
level=error ts=2026-03-18T09:12:34Z caller=remote.go:313 component=remote write err="Post \"https://rw-gateway.eu-west1.redwood:9201/write\": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)"
```
Jia: interestingly the spike aligns with the SNI-routing change that landed in prod ~09:10. ops-team rotated the gateway pool and enabled multiplexing by cluster-id. possible fanout to older backends?
Tom: i saw the same across ~12 pods. metrics show per-scrape latency p99 jumped from ~120ms -> 2.3s and then remote_write queue length grew.
sre-bot: incident created: SGD-2026-03-18-018. alerts fired: prom_scrape_duration_seconds{job="node-exporter"} p99 >= 2s, prom_remote_write_errors_total > 20
Ashish: quick triage ideas -- 1) SNI routing misconfig could throw traffic to an overloaded rw instance which then acts like a blackhole. 2) relabeling got accidentally relaxed and now node-exporter is sending high-card metrics (k8s_pod:ip label leak) causing serialization/backpressure. 3) tls handshake / keepalive issues with new muxing.
Margo: i dumped samples from the queue and saw many series with label pod_ip and pod_id garbage. cardinality looks ~10x normal for a subset of nodes.
Jia: can you grep relabel_configs for node-exporter job? maybe someone removed pod IP drop.
Margo: found it in prod:
```yaml
- job_name: node-exporter
  static_configs: ...
  relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_ip]
      action: keep
      regex: ""
```
Margo: that keep with empty regex was a bad rollback from an unrelated change -> basically kept pod_ip. earlier we had a drop that removed pod_ip from exported labels.
Tom: that explains the cardinality spike. but why the proxied 504s? overloaded rw due to sudden multiplier of series + some backend got hit harder because SNI hash moved traffic unevenly.
Ashish: plan: 1) revert the relabel -> drop pod_ip (hotfix now) 2) scale up rw-gateway pool instances temporarily + re-balance 3) add a short-term reject rule on proxy to rate-limit new series ingestion by src cluster to avoid long tails.
Jia: agreed. also we should increase scrape_timeout for node-exporter to avoid client cancels while the queue drains (but carefully; we don't want to mask root cause).
Margo: performing relabel rollback now. pushing patch to prometheus-configs -> apply.
Tom: i'll add 4 more rw-gateway replicas and pin them off the old SNI mapping to spread load. also toggling muxing fallback to preserved behavior.
sre-bot: change-approved: prometheus-configs@infra, scale-request submitted to k8s-autoscaler, rw-gateway replicas requested.
Margo: hotfix rolled: relabel reverted. initial queue depth dropped ~40% within 90s. p99 scrape latency back to ~180ms.
Ashish: nice. follow-ups: - audit PRs that touch relabels (add CI check that rejects empty keep regex) - add an alert for sudden per-job series_count increase (delta over 1m) - add SNI routing canary for muxing changes (traffic simulation)
Jia: i'll own the relabel CI check. Tom can you own the SNI canary?
Tom: yup. also adding a dashboard panel: remote_write_outstanding_series and per-backend fanout to identify hotspots.
Margo: filing a postmortem draft. high-level: cascading effect from two unrelated changes (relabel rollback + SNI muxing) produced fanout-cardinality spike -> remote_write backpressure -> scrape tail latency and 504s.
Ashish: TL;DR: don't mix routing & label-change rollouts at the same time :sweat_smile:
Margo: thanks all. will ping when postmortem link is up. :thumbsup:
